the relationship between alcohol and blood pressure in an untreated population of men and women.
the effect of alcohol consumption on blood pressure in a population of middle-aged men and women who were not treated for hypertension during the 20-year follow-up period.
the effects of moderate alcohol consumption in a population free of antihypertensive medication and without a history of myocardial infarction.

low and moderate alcohol intake in men is not associated with a reduction in blood pressure, and that the evidence in women is not conclusive.

the relationship between alcohol and cardiovascular risk is U-shaped, and that this relationship depends upon the presence of cardiovascular risk factors.
alcohol intake in the low to moderate range is associated with a lower blood pressure and that the association is stronger for systolic than diastolic blood pressure.
